classes.objetivo: Distinguir entre contar una emoción y mostrarla con acciones, reacciones del cuerpo y detalles de los sentidos, y repasar used to y would para hábitos del pasado.

ensenanza.en: Her hands began to tremble as she opened the letter, and she had to read the first line three times.
ensenanza.es: Las manos le empezaron a temblar al abrir la carta, y tuvo que leer la primera línea tres veces.
ensenanza.nota: Muestra el nervio con una reacción del cuerpo, sin decir «she was nervous».

ensenanza.en: He slammed the door so hard that the glasses on the shelf rattled, and nobody dared to say a word.
ensenanza.es: Dio un portazo tan fuerte que los vasos de la estantería tintinearon, y nadie se atrevió a decir nada.
ensenanza.nota: La acción y el sonido muestran la rabia sin nombrarla.

ensenanza.en: Across the table, Leo would fidget with his spoon and avoid eye contact whenever the subject of money came up.
ensenanza.es: Al otro lado de la mesa, Leo jugueteaba con la cuchara y evitaba mirar a los ojos cada vez que salía el tema del dinero.
ensenanza.nota: Would + verbo base describe una conducta repetida en el pasado; los gestos muestran la incomodidad.

ensenanza.en: When he was angry, my grandfather would clench his fists and count the seconds under his breath before answering.
ensenanza.es: Cuando se enojaba, mi abuelo apretaba los puños y contaba los segundos en voz baja antes de contestar.
ensenanza.nota: Dos acciones concretas muestran el autocontrol; contar sería «he tried to stay calm».

ensenanza.en: When burnt toast fills a silent kitchen, add a lump in your throat and readers feel the tension without being told.
ensenanza.es: Cuando la tostada quemada llena una cocina en silencio, añade un nudo en la garganta y los lectores sentirán la tensión sin que se la cuenten.
ensenanza.nota: Un detalle del olfato, el silencio y una sensación del cuerpo muestran la tensión.

ensenanza.en: If you fidget, bite your nails and keep checking the clock, readers feel your anxiety without ever being told about it.
ensenanza.es: Si te mueves sin parar, te muerdes las uñas y miras el reloj todo el tiempo, los lectores sienten tu ansiedad sin que nadie se la cuente.
ensenanza.nota: Varias acciones pequeñas y concretas muestran una emoción mejor que una palabra abstracta.

explicacion.texto: Contar (tell) nombra la emoción: She was nervous. Mostrar (show) da lo que el lector vería, oiría u olería, y le deja deducir la emoción: Her hands began to tremble; She bit her nails. Usa acciones concretas, reacciones del cuerpo y detalles de los cinco sentidos, y evita los tópicos. Contar sigue siendo útil para resumir tiempo o información. Para hábitos y fondo de la escena en pasado, repasa used to (estados y hábitos: The house used to smell of pine) y would (solo acciones repetidas: We would sit on the wall).

formula.nota: objeto concreto que el lector puede ver

filas.texto: He slammed the door so hard that the glasses rattled.
The smell of burnt milk filled the kitchen.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: His hands were shaking of anger.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: His hands were shaking with anger.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: La causa de una reacción del cuerpo se introduce con with: shaking with anger, no «of» (calco de «de rabia»).

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: We would live in a small flat when I was a child.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: We used to live in a small flat when I was a child.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Live es un estado, no una acción que se repite: con estados se usa used to; would solo sirve para acciones repetidas.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Leo corrigen el relato de Leo para un taller de escritura.

dialogo.texto: You wrote, “She was nervous.” Can you show it instead?
dialogo.traduccion: Escribiste «Estaba nerviosa». ¿Puedes mostrarlo en su lugar?

dialogo.texto: Sure. Her hands began to tremble as she opened the letter.
dialogo.traduccion: Claro. Las manos le empezaron a temblar al abrir la carta.

dialogo.texto: Better! Now I can see it. What about the old house?
dialogo.traduccion: ¡Mejor! Ahora lo veo. ¿Y la casa vieja?

dialogo.texto: It used to smell of pine and wet wool. We would sit by the fire every evening.
dialogo.traduccion: Solía oler a pino y a lana mojada. Nos sentábamos junto al fuego cada tarde.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué cambió Leo para mostrar el nervio?

opciones.es: Escribió una reacción del cuerpo: le temblaban las manos.

item.feedback: Leo sustituyó «She was nervous» por «Her hands began to tremble…»: una reacción del cuerpo que el lector puede ver, en lugar de nombrar la emoción.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase muestra la rabia de Tom en lugar de contarla?
guiada.texto: In a writing workshop, the teacher asks the students to replace the line “Tom was angry” with something the reader can see or hear, without naming the emotion.
opciones: Tom slammed the door so hard that the glasses rattled.
Tom was so angry that he could not speak.
Tom's anger was obvious to everybody in the room.
guiada.feedback: El portazo y el tintineo de los vasos son una acción y un sonido que el lector percibe; las otras frases siguen nombrando la emoción.
guiada.pista: Busca la acción concreta con sonido, no la etiqueta «angry».

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Su voz empezó a temblar de enojo al leer el mensaje en voz alta.»
guiada.texto: Sara did not shout. Her voice began to tremble ___ anger as she read the message aloud, and nobody in the room moved.
guiada.feedback: La causa de una reacción del cuerpo se introduce normalmente con with: tremble with anger. «Of» sería un calco del español; in anger también se oye, pero with es la forma habitual.
guiada.pista: La preposición que introduce la causa de una reacción.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Solía contar los segundos hasta que pasaba el tren nocturno.»
guiada.respuesta: He would count the seconds until the night train passed
guiada.feedback: Would + verbo base describe una conducta repetida en el pasado; count the seconds se mantiene junto como colocación.
guiada.pista: Would va seguido del verbo base, sin to.
aceptadas: Until the night train passed, he would count the seconds

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con lo que hace el narrador.
pares: Her hands trembled as she opened the letter.
Muestra nervios con el cuerpo
He slammed the door so hard that the windows rattled.
Muestra rabia con acción y sonido
The smell of burnt toast filled the silent kitchen.
Muestra tensión con olor y silencio
She was very nervous about the exam.
Cuenta la emoción sin mostrarla
practica.feedback: Las tres primeras ofrecen detalles que el lector percibe; la última nombra la emoción y por eso cuenta.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué emoción muestra la escena sin nombrarla.
practica.audio: The kitchen smelled of burnt toast. Nobody spoke. Leo sat with his coat still on, tapping the table, and Ana kept her eyes on the clock. When the phone finally rang, neither of them moved. Leo took a long breath, and his hand, just for a moment, began to tremble.
opciones: Anxious waiting for news that may change everything.
Quiet sadness after a painful argument.
Bored waiting while dinner is being prepared.
Hidden anger that one of them cannot express.
practica.feedback: El silencio, el reloj, el teléfono que nadie coge y la mano que tiembla muestran ansiedad ante una noticia esperada; ninguna frase nombra la emoción.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Se mordía las uñas y evitaba mirar a los ojos.»
practica.respuesta: She bit her nails and avoided eye contact
practica.feedback: Dos acciones concretas muestran incomodidad; avoid eye contact se mantiene junto como colocación.

evaluacion.consigna: Reescribe las tres frases mostrando la emoción con una acción o un gesto.
evaluacion.texto: Frases que cuentan: «Leo was embarrassed. Mia was nervous. Ana was angry.» Reescríbelas mostrando cada emoción con una acción, un gesto o una reacción del cuerpo (sin usar embarrassed, nervous ni angry).
evaluacion.respuesta: Leo stared at the floor and avoided eye contact as everybody laughed. Mia bit her nails, tapped her foot and read the same line of the letter three times. Ana slammed the door so hard that the glasses rattled.
aceptadas: Leo looked away and said nothing while the others laughed. Mia began to fidget, and her hands started to tremble as she checked the clock. Ana clenched her fists and slammed the door behind her.
Leo kept his eyes on the floor while the room laughed. Mia kept checking the clock, and she began to bite her nails. Ana slammed her hand on the table and left the room.
evaluacion.feedback: Mostrar es dar un gesto o una reacción concreta: Leo mirando al suelo; Mia mordiéndose las uñas o mirando el reloj; Ana con un portazo o los puños apretados.

evidencias: kept his eyes on the floor

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el detalle de los puños apretados.
evaluacion.audio: The house was silent except for the clock in the hall. Carlos waited by the window with his jacket still on, although he had been home for an hour. On the table, his coffee had gone cold. Every few minutes he picked up the phone, looked at it and put it down again. When his daughter finally came in, he started to speak, and stopped. She smiled. He let out a breath that seemed to have been waiting all day, and only then did he notice that his fists were clenched.
opciones: That he had been tense all day without noticing it.
That he was angry with his daughter for coming home late.
That he was trying to hide his anger from her.
That he was still cross with her for not calling.
evaluacion.feedback: El aliento retenido y «only then did he notice» indican una tensión acumulada de la que no era consciente; la sonrisa de ella lo libera. El texto no habla de enojo.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Nadie podía ignorar el olor a tostada quemada que venía de la cocina.»
evaluacion.texto: It was a small flat, and nobody could ignore the smell of ___ toast that drifted in from the kitchen while the argument went on.
evaluacion.feedback: Burnt toast es el detalle sensorial clásico para una tensión que nadie menciona; burned es la variante americana y burning toast también es natural.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere el comentario de la profesora sobre el primer borrador?
evaluacion.texto: Mia's first draft read: “Sara was very nervous. She was worried about the interview. She was sad because her father could not come. She was also angry with herself.” Her teacher wrote on the page: “Four emotions, and I don't feel any of them.”
opciones: That naming emotions is weaker than showing what causes them.
That a character should never feel more than one emotion.
That the draft needs fewer details about the interview.
That Sara's father should appear in the scene.
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora no discute las emociones, sino que el lector no las siente: nombrarlas no basta, hay que mostrar lo que las provoca y lo que hacen.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere el último detalle del narrador sobre la casa?
repaso.texto: When we were children, the house used to be full of the scent of pine and wet wool, and my mother would hum while she counted the seconds on the kitchen clock. Now it smells of nothing at all. My father keeps the windows shut, even in July, and nobody hums.
opciones: That something painful has changed in the family.
That the father has become very strict about cleaning.
That the children no longer want to visit the house.
That the house has simply been cleaned from top to bottom.
repaso.feedback: El contraste entre el pasado (olor, tarareo) y el presente (nada, ventanas cerradas, nadie tararea) sugiere una pérdida sin nombrarla.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué acepta ahora la profesora el texto de Leo.
repaso.audio: Leo showed his teacher his first draft: Mia was angry. The teacher sighed. “Show me,” she said. So Leo wrote it again: Mia got up so fast that her chair fell over, picked up her bag and left without a word. The teacher read it twice. “Now I believe you,” she said. “I can see the anger, and you never even used the word.”
opciones: Because the reader now sees the anger instead of being told.
Because the new version is longer than the first draft.
Because Mia's action is more polite than her first reaction.
Because Leo has chosen a stronger word than angry.
repaso.feedback: La profesora lo dice con sus palabras: ve la rabia y Leo ni siquiera usó la palabra. Mostrar convence más que nombrar.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Contábamos los segundos hasta que sonaba el timbre.»
repaso.texto: At the end of the lesson we used to ___ the seconds until the bell rang, and our teacher would pretend not to notice.
repaso.feedback: Count the seconds es la colocación que se usa para esperar con impaciencia; used to + verbo base marca el hábito del pasado.

classes.objetivo: Controlar el ritmo narrativo con anteposición de lugar (Down the hill ran the dog), adverbios negativos con inversión (Never had she seen…), fragmentos intencionados y frases de longitud variada.

ensenanza.en: Down the hill ran the dog, and behind it, carried on the wind, came the distant barking of another.
ensenanza.es: Colina abajo corrió el perro, y detrás de él, llevados por el viento, llegaron los ladridos lejanos de otro.
ensenanza.nota: Anteposición: lugar + verbo + sujeto. El sujeto es un nombre (the dog), así que el verbo va antes.

ensenanza.en: On the table lay a single letter, and beside it, in the half-dark, lay the key nobody had touched for years.
ensenanza.es: Sobre la mesa yacía una sola carta, y junto a ella, en la penumbra, estaba la llave que nadie había tocado en años.
ensenanza.nota: Con verbos de posición como lay, stood o hung la inversión es natural: lugar + verbo + sujeto.

ensenanza.en: Up the stairs came muffled footsteps, and every step made the old boards creak as though the house were complaining.
ensenanza.es: Escaleras arriba llegaron unos pasos apagados, y cada paso hacía crujir las viejas tablas como si la casa se quejara.
ensenanza.nota: Los sonidos se prestan a la anteposición: el lector oye primero el lugar y después el sujeto.

ensenanza.en: Motionless she stood at the gate, and in the whole lane there was not a soul to hear her call.
ensenanza.es: Inmóvil se quedó junto a la verja, y en todo el camino no había ni un alma que oyera su llamada.
ensenanza.nota: Si el sujeto es un pronombre no hay inversión: Motionless she stood. El adjetivo al inicio pone el énfasis en el estado.

ensenanza.en: Never had he known a deathly silence like that one; out of nowhere, the whole hill seemed to fall silent.
ensenanza.es: Nunca había conocido un silencio sepulcral como ese; de repente, toda la colina parecía quedarse callada.
ensenanza.nota: Never al inicio pide inversión: never + auxiliar + sujeto (had he).

ensenanza.en: She walked for hours through the empty streets, chilled to the bones, and found only an eerie calm. Then she stopped.
ensenanza.es: Caminó durante horas por las calles vacías, helada hasta los huesos, y solo encontró una calma inquietante. Entonces se detuvo.
ensenanza.nota: Una frase larga que fluye y una corta que golpea crean ritmo; la corta funciona como un fragmento.

explicacion.texto: En la narrativa, el inglés altera el orden normal para dar ritmo. Anteposición de lugar: Down the hill ran the dog; si el sujeto es un nombre, el verbo va antes (ran the dog), pero con pronombre no hay inversión (Down the hill it ran). Un adverbio negativo al inicio pide auxiliar + sujeto: Never had she seen such a view. Los fragmentos sin verbo (Silence. Then footsteps.) crean tensión. Alterna frases largas con una corta que golpea. Si los usas en cada frase, pierden efecto.

formula.nota: el verbo va antes del sujeto
sujeto: un nombre, no un pronombre

filas.texto: The dog ran down the hill.
Down the hill ran the dog.
A letter lay on the table.
On the table lay a letter.
She had never seen such a view.
Never had she seen such a view.

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con un pronombre como sujeto no hay inversión: lugar + pronombre + verbo.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Never she had seen such a place.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Never had she seen such a place.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Tras never al inicio, el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: never had she. El orden «never she had» es un calco del español.

situacion.contexto: Tom le enseña a Mia un párrafo de su relato y ella le sugiere cambios de ritmo.

dialogo.texto: I wrote: A dog ran down the hill. There was silence. Then I heard footsteps.
dialogo.traduccion: Escribí: Un perro corrió colina abajo. Hubo silencio. Luego oí pasos.

dialogo.texto: Try this: Down the hill ran the dog. Silence. Then footsteps.
dialogo.traduccion: Prueba esto: Colina abajo corrió el perro. Silencio. Luego, pasos.

dialogo.texto: Why no verb after silence?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Por qué no hay verbo después de silence?

dialogo.texto: One short word makes the moment tense. But don't do it every time.
dialogo.traduccion: Una palabra corta hace el momento más tenso. Pero no lo hagas siempre.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿para qué sirve el fragmento «Silence.»?

opciones.es: Para crear tensión en un momento concreto.
Para explicar una regla de gramática.

item.feedback: Mia dice que un fragmento corto hace el momento tenso, y añade que no se debe usar siempre.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Por el sendero subieron unos pasos apagados.»
guiada.respuesta: Up the path came muffled footsteps
guiada.feedback: Lugar + verbo + sujeto: el sujeto es un nombre (muffled footsteps), así que came va antes de él.
guiada.pista: Empieza por el lugar; el verbo precede al sujeto.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué versión antepone correctamente el lugar cuando el sujeto es «it»?
guiada.texto: Mia is revising a scene in which her dog gets out of the gate and runs down the lane. Because the subject will be the pronoun it, she has to choose the right word order.
opciones: Down the lane it ran, barking at nothing.
Down the lane ran it, barking at nothing.
Down it the lane ran, barking at nothing.
Down the lane did it run, barking at nothing.
guiada.feedback: Con un pronombre como sujeto no hay inversión: lugar + pronombre + verbo. Las demás versiones alteran el orden sin motivo.
guiada.pista: Con pronombre, el sujeto va antes del verbo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Nunca había visto una calle tan silenciosa.»
guiada.texto: The cold reached her bones as she crossed the square. Never ___ she seen such a silent street, and not a soul was around.
guiada.feedback: Never al inicio exige auxiliar + sujeto: never had she seen. Sin la inversión la frase sería un calco del español.
guiada.pista: Tras never, el auxiliar del past perfect va antes del sujeto.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con el recurso de ritmo que usa.
pares: Down the hill ran the dog.
Anteposición de lugar con inversión
Down the hill it ran.
Anteposición con pronombre, sin inversión
Never had she seen such a view.
Adverbio negativo + auxiliar + sujeto
Silence. Then footsteps.
Fragmentos que crean tensión
practica.feedback: Cada frase altera el orden de una manera distinta: inversión con nombre, pronombre sin inversión, adverbio negativo y fragmentos.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué efecto crean las frases cortas del final.
practica.audio: She walked for hours through the empty streets, past closed shops and dark windows, until the cold reached her bones. Then she stopped. Silence. A dog, somewhere far off. And then, slowly, footsteps. She did not look back.
opciones: They slow the pace and build tension after the long sentence.
They add more information about the streets she crossed.
They suggest that the narrator is tired of describing.
They explain why she had walked for hours.
practica.feedback: La frase larga fluye como el paseo; las cortas (Silence. A dog… footsteps.) frenan el ritmo y crean tensión. No añaden datos ni explican nada.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Inmóvil, se quedó junto a la verja, sin un alma alrededor.»
practica.respuesta: Motionless she stood at the gate, not a soul around
aceptadas: She stood motionless at the gate, not a soul around
practica.feedback: Con pronombre no hay inversión (Motionless she stood); el adjetivo al inicio da énfasis, aunque también es posible colocarlo tras el verbo.

evaluacion.consigna: Reescribe el párrafo con anteposición de lugar, never + inversión y dos fragmentos.
evaluacion.texto: Párrafo: «A young woman stood at the gate. The old dog ran up the hill. She had never heard such a silent night. There was silence. Then there was a creak.» Reescríbelo con una anteposición de lugar con inversión, una frase con Never had y dos fragmentos sin verbo.
evaluacion.respuesta: At the gate stood a young woman. Up the hill ran the old dog. Never had she heard such a silent night. Silence. Then a creak.
aceptadas: By the gate stood a young woman. Up the hill raced the old dog. Never before had she heard such a silent night. Silence. A creak.
evaluacion.feedback: El párrafo mejora con lugar + verbo + sujeto (At the gate stood…), never + inversión (Never had she heard…) y dos fragmentos que golpean (Silence. Then a creak.).

evidencias: silence then the sound of a creak

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el cambio de ritmo al final del pasaje.
evaluacion.audio: The group had been climbing since dawn, and by midday the top of the hill had disappeared into cloud. Up the path they walked, step after tired step, each of them chilled to the bones, each of them counting the hours until camp. Below them, the valley had vanished completely, and the path behind them was already gone. Nobody spoke. Then, out of nowhere, the wind dropped. A deathly silence. Somewhere above them, a rock fell. Another. Motionless, they listened. Carlos was the first to move. He raised one hand and whispered a single word. Down.
opciones: That the group senses a danger it cannot yet see.
That the group has finally reached the safety of camp.
That the group is arguing about which way to go.
That the danger is over now that the wind has dropped.
evaluacion.feedback: Las frases largas reflejan la marcha monótona; al final, los fragmentos (A deathly silence. Another. Down.), el viento que cae y las piedras que se desprenden anuncian un peligro que el grupo aún no ve. Nadie discute y nada indica que el peligro haya pasado.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Apenas había cerrado la puerta cuando se apagaron las luces.»
evaluacion.texto: It was past midnight, and the flat was quiet. Hardly ___ she closed the door when every light in the building went out.
evaluacion.feedback: Hardly al inicio exige la misma inversión que never: hardly had she closed… when. El past perfect marca lo anterior.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito termina el autor con una frase muy corta?
evaluacion.texto: She had spent three years planning the route, saving every spare cent, studying the maps until she could have drawn them from memory, and telling nobody, not even her sister, what she intended to do with the money. On the morning of the departure, the suitcase was already packed. She did not go.
opciones: To surprise the reader with an unexpected twist.
To confirm that she had prepared everything well.
To hint that her sister had talked her out of it.
To summarise the long preparation in a short phrase.
evaluacion.feedback: La frase larga acumula preparativos y la corta los contradice: el contraste de ritmo produce un giro inesperado. El texto no menciona a la hermana.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Nunca antes había oído un silencio tan profundo.»
repaso.respuesta: Never before had I heard such a deep silence
repaso.feedback: Never before al inicio pide inversión: auxiliar + sujeto (had I). El énfasis recae en lo excepcional de la experiencia.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué efecto logran las anteposiciones de este fragmento?
repaso.texto: The party was going well when the music stopped. At the door stood a man nobody had invited. Never had the room been so quiet. Slowly, he took off his hat. Then, in a voice that seemed to come from another age, he asked for a glass of water.
opciones: They delay the subject and focus attention on the stranger.
They speed the scene up by cutting extra words.
They show that the guests know the stranger well.
They reveal that the narrator is one of the guests.
repaso.feedback: La inversión (At the door stood…, Never had the room…) retrasa el sujeto y lo destaca: el lector se centra en el desconocido y en el silencio.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Toda la calle se quedó callada al pasar el desconocido.»
repaso.texto: The whole street seemed to fall ___ as the stranger walked past, and nobody dared to ask him who he was.
repaso.feedback: Fall silent es la colocación para quedarse callado de pronto; fall quiet también es posible, pero es más coloquial.

classes.objetivo: Reconstruir el orden real de los hechos en una anécdota que salta entre tiempos, distinguiendo la línea principal del fondo anterior y de lo que sucedería después.

ensenanza.en: Years earlier, her father had promised to take her to the city, and she had never forgotten it.
ensenanza.es: Años antes, su padre le había prometido llevarla a la ciudad, y ella nunca lo había olvidado.
ensenanza.nota: Past perfect (had promised): un hecho anterior al momento que se cuenta; years earlier lo señala.

ensenanza.en: By the time the last train arrived, my grandmother had been waiting on the station platform for her cousin for nearly two hours.
ensenanza.es: Para cuando llegó el último tren, mi abuela llevaba casi dos horas esperando a su prima en el andén de la estación.
ensenanza.nota: Past perfect continuous (had been waiting): una actividad en curso antes del hecho principal (arrived).

ensenanza.en: A stranger offered her his umbrella, and they talked until the rain stopped and the lamps came on along the street.
ensenanza.es: Un desconocido le ofreció su paraguas, y hablaron hasta que dejó de llover y se encendieron las farolas de la calle.
ensenanza.nota: Los hechos principales van en past simple y en orden: offered, talked, stopped, came on.

ensenanza.en: She did not know it then, but she would marry him three years later, and they would tie the knot in the village church.
ensenanza.es: Entonces no lo sabía, pero se casaría con él tres años después, y darían el sí en la iglesia del pueblo.
ensenanza.nota: Would + verbo anticipa lo posterior al momento del relato, visto desde el pasado.

ensenanza.en: As it turned out, the stranger was her cousin's friend, a fact that would only come to light at the wedding.
ensenanza.es: Como resultó ser, el desconocido era amigo de su prima, algo que solo saldría a la luz en la boda.
ensenanza.nota: As it turned out presenta un hecho sorprendente que cambia lo que el oyente creía saber.

ensenanza.en: When the old man was about to pass away, he asked the family to keep the umbrella that had started the whole story.
ensenanza.es: Cuando el anciano estaba a punto de fallecer, pidió a la familia que conservara el paraguas que había comenzado toda la historia.
ensenanza.nota: Was about to + verbo base: estaba a punto de; had started sitúa el paraguas antes de ese momento.

explicacion.titulo: Saltos en el tiempo de una anécdota
explicacion.texto: Una anécdota casi nunca va en orden. La línea principal se cuenta en pasado simple (arrived, gave, talked). Lo anterior va en pasado perfecto (had promised, had told) y lo que ya duraba antes de un hecho, en pasado perfecto continuo (had been waiting). Lo posterior, visto desde el pasado, con would + verbo (she would marry him). Los marcadores ayudan: years earlier, by the time, three years later. Para reconstruir el orden real, ordena por tiempo verbal y marcadores, no por el orden en que aparece cada frase.

formula.texto: By the time the train arrived,

filas.texto: Actividad en curso antes del hecho

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: When I arrived, she was cooking for three hours.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: When I arrived, she had been cooking for three hours.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Was cooking no expresa una duración que llega hasta un momento pasado. Para eso se usa had been + -ing.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: After she had arrived, she had sat down and had opened the letter.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: After she had arrived, she sat down and opened the letter.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Una vez fijado el momento anterior con had arrived, los hechos siguientes vuelven al pasado simple.

situacion.contexto: Leo le pregunta a su hermana Ana cómo se conocieron sus abuelos.

dialogo.texto: Ana, how did Grandma meet Grandpa?
dialogo.traduccion: Ana, ¿cómo conoció la abuela al abuelo?

dialogo.texto: It was 1962. She had been waiting at the station for two hours.
dialogo.traduccion: Era 1962. Llevaba dos horas esperando en la estación.

dialogo.texto: Two hours? Why?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Dos horas? ¿Por qué?

dialogo.texto: Her cousin's train was late. Then a stranger gave her his umbrella.
dialogo.traduccion: El tren de su prima llegaba tarde. Entonces un desconocido le dio su paraguas.

dialogo.texto: Was that Grandpa?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Ese era el abuelo?

dialogo.texto: It was. She didn't know it then, but she would marry him three years later.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Entonces no lo sabía, pero se casaría con él tres años después.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿cuánto tiempo llevaba esperando la abuela cuando apareció el desconocido?
item.feedback: Ana dice «She had been waiting at the station for two hours»: esa duración llega hasta el momento en que el desconocido le dio el paraguas. Los tres años son hasta la boda.

guiada.consigna: Según este fragmento, ¿qué ocurrió primero en la cronología real?
guiada.texto: By the time the last train arrived, my grandmother had been waiting on the station platform for two hours. Years earlier, her father had promised to take her to the city. A stranger offered her his umbrella, and they talked until the rain stopped.
opciones: Her father promised to take her to the city.
She waited for two hours on the platform.
A stranger offered her his umbrella.
The last train arrived at the station.
guiada.feedback: Years earlier y el past perfect (had promised) sitúan la promesa antes de todo lo demás; la espera, el tren y el paraguas son posteriores.
guiada.pista: Busca el marcador que lleva más atrás en el tiempo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Cuando llegó el autobús, Sara llevaba dos horas esperando.»
guiada.texto: By the time the bus arrived, Sara ___ been waiting for two hours, and her feet were frozen.
guiada.feedback: Had been waiting expresa una actividad en curso antes de un hecho pasado (arrived): past perfect continuous.
guiada.pista: Auxiliar del past perfect continuous: ___ been + -ing.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Años antes, su abuelo había prometido llevarla a la costa.»
guiada.respuesta: Years earlier, her grandfather had promised to take her to the coast
guiada.feedback: Years earlier abre la frase para situar el hecho antes de la línea principal; had promised es el past perfect correspondiente.
guiada.pista: El marcador de tiempo va primero; had + participio después del sujeto.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con su lugar en la historia.
pares: The train arrived.
Línea principal del relato
Her father had promised to take her.
Hecho anterior a la línea principal
She had been waiting for two hours.
Actividad en curso antes del hecho
She would marry him three years later.
Futuro visto desde el pasado
practica.feedback: Cada forma verbal indica dónde se sitúa el hecho respecto a la línea principal: pasado simple, past perfect, past perfect continuous y would.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué había pasado antes de que ella conociera al desconocido.
practica.audio: I must have been about twenty. By the time the last train arrived, I had been waiting on the platform for nearly two hours, because my cousin's train had been delayed by snow. Years earlier, my father had promised to take me to the city, and I suppose I wanted to prove that I could manage alone. Then a stranger offered me his umbrella. I did not know it then, but I would marry him three years later.
opciones: Her cousin's train had been delayed, so she had waited for hours.
Her father had already taken her to the city twice.
She had married the stranger three years earlier.
Her cousin had lent her an umbrella before the rain.
practica.feedback: El retraso del tren de su prima y las dos horas de espera son anteriores al encuentro; la promesa del padre sigue sin cumplirse y la boda es posterior.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Entonces no lo sabía, pero se casaría con él y vivirían cincuenta años allí.»
practica.texto: She did not know it then, but she ___ marry him three years later and live in the same village for fifty years.
practica.feedback: Would + verbo base anticipa, desde el pasado, algo que ocurrirá después de la escena que se cuenta.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué el abuelo nunca devolvió el reloj.
evaluacion.audio: My grandfather rarely talked about his youth, so it was a surprise when, at a family party, he handed me a small silver watch. “Your great-grandmother gave it to me the night I left the village,” he said. “By then, she had been saving for it for over a year, and she made me promise to bring it back. As it turned out, I never returned it: she passed away before I came home. That watch would stay in my pocket for sixty years. Now it is yours.” I had never seen him so serious. The room went quiet, and even the children stopped playing.
opciones: He could not keep his promise because she died before his return.
He lost it soon after he left and kept that a secret.
He preferred to keep it, since it reminded him of his village.
She had asked him to give it to his own children.
evaluacion.feedback: El abuelo había prometido devolver el reloj, pero su madre falleció antes de que él volviera (passed away before I came home): la promesa quedó imposible de cumplir.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige el orden real de los hechos de la tía.
evaluacion.audio: My aunt was waiting at the airport when the announcement came. By then she had been sitting there for five hours. Three months earlier she had quit her job, and years before that she had promised her mother that she would one day return to the island. When the plane finally landed, she stood up and, as it turned out, she would never leave the island again.
opciones: She promised her mother, she quit her job, she waited at the airport.
She quit her job, she promised her mother, she waited at the airport.
She waited at the airport, she quit her job, she promised her mother.
She promised her mother, she waited at the airport, she quit her job.
evaluacion.feedback: Years before that es lo más antiguo (la promesa), three months earlier sitúa la renuncia después, y la espera de cinco horas es lo más reciente.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los abuelos de Ana se casaron en 1965, en una iglesia que ya no existe.»
evaluacion.texto: Ana's grandparents ___ the knot in 1965, in a small village church that no longer exists, and nobody in the family has ever found the photographs.
evaluacion.feedback: Tie the knot es la expresión coloquial para casarse; aquí va en pasado simple porque el hecho pertenece a la línea principal.

evaluacion.consigna: Une en una frase: Sara llevaba dos horas esperando cuando llegó el tren.
evaluacion.texto: Dos hechos: Sara esperó en el andén durante dos horas. Después llegó el tren de su prima. Escribe una sola frase en inglés que diga que, cuando llegó el tren de su prima, Sara llevaba dos horas esperando.
evaluacion.respuesta: By the time her cousin's train arrived, Sara had been waiting for two hours.
aceptadas: When her cousin's train arrived, Sara had been waiting for two hours.
Sara had been waiting for two hours by the time her cousin's train arrived.
Sara had been waiting for two hours when her cousin's train arrived.
evaluacion.feedback: La frase destaca el hecho principal (arrived) y el fondo anterior con duración (had been waiting for two hours).

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué actitud muestra la tía ante lo que ha descubierto?
repaso.texto: Dear Leo, something has come to light while I was clearing Grandma's kitchen. Do you remember the old box where she kept her recipes? I always assumed they were hers. As it turned out, half of them were written by a woman none of us had heard of, and Grandma had copied them out for sixty years without a word. I'm not upset. I just wonder what else she never told us.
opciones: Curious and a little wistful about what Grandma kept to herself.
Angry that Grandma kept a secret from the family.
Anxious that more secrets will damage the family.
Happy that the secret turned out to be so small.
repaso.feedback: «I'm not upset» descarta el enojo, y «I just wonder what else she never told us» muestra curiosidad con cierta nostalgia; no hay preocupación por la familia ni alegría.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Para cuando llegó el tren, ella llevaba dos horas esperando.»
repaso.respuesta: By the time the train arrived, she had been waiting for two hours
aceptadas: She had been waiting for two hours by the time the train arrived
repaso.feedback: El hecho principal (arrived) va en past simple y el fondo con duración en past perfect continuous; las dos cláusulas pueden intercambiar su lugar.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Años antes, su padre le había prometido llevarla, pero nunca lo hizo.»
repaso.texto: Years ___, her father had promised to take her to the city, but he never did, and she had stopped asking him.
repaso.feedback: Years earlier (o years before) sitúa el hecho antes del momento que se cuenta y justifica el past perfect had promised.

classes.objetivo: Redactar una anécdota con escena de fondo, un hecho que la rompe, una intención interrumpida (was about to, was going to), un giro y un desenlace anticipado con would.

vocabulario.es: yo no tenía ni idea de que

ensenanza.en: The café was nearly empty, and the rain was tapping on the windows as I stirred a coffee that had long gone cold.
ensenanza.es: La cafetería estaba casi vacía, y la lluvia golpeteaba las ventanas mientras yo removía un café que ya se había enfriado.
ensenanza.nota: Past continuous para el fondo de la escena: was tapping, con detalles que el lector percibe.

ensenanza.en: Suddenly, a woman sat down at my table, and I noticed that my wallet was no longer on the counter.
ensenanza.es: De repente, una mujer se sentó a mi mesa, y noté que mi cartera ya no estaba en el mostrador.
ensenanza.nota: Suddenly + past simple: el hecho que rompe la escena.

ensenanza.en: I was about to pay when it dawned on me that my wallet was gone, and my face went hot.
ensenanza.es: Iba a pagar cuando caí en la cuenta de que mi cartera había desaparecido, y la cara se me puso roja.
ensenanza.nota: Was about to + verbo base: estaba a punto de; se interrumpe con un hecho en past simple.

ensenanza.en: I was going to call the police, but then the woman smiled and handed back my wallet, still warm from her pocket.
ensenanza.es: Iba a llamar a la policía, pero entonces la mujer sonrió y me devolvió la cartera, todavía tibia del bolsillo.
ensenanza.nota: Was going to + verbo: intención en el pasado que no se cumple; but then introduce el giro.

ensenanza.en: Little did I know that the stranger returning my wallet would become my business partner within a year.
ensenanza.es: Yo no tenía ni idea de que la desconocida que me devolvía la cartera se convertiría en mi socia en menos de un año.
ensenanza.nota: Little al inicio pide inversión (did I know) y would anticipa el desenlace.

ensenanza.en: As luck would have it, the wallet had not been stolen; by a twist of fate, it had fallen into kind hands, to my relief.
ensenanza.es: Quiso la suerte que la cartera no hubiera sido robada; por un capricho del destino, había caído en buenas manos, para mi alivio.
ensenanza.nota: El giro cambia lo que el lector creía; had been / had fallen sitúan lo ocurrido antes.

explicacion.texto: Una anécdota con giro tiene tres partes. Escena: el fondo en pasado continuo con detalles (The rain was tapping on the windows). Hecho y giro: algo la rompe en pasado simple (Suddenly, a woman sat down), a menudo con una intención que no se cumple o una acción interrumpida: I was about to pay when… / I was going to call the police, but then… Desenlace: se anticipa con would, y tras little se invierte: Little did I know that she would become my partner. Sigue el orden escena → hecho → giro → desenlace.

formula.nota: intención a punto de cumplirse: was about to + verbo base

formula.texto: I realised my wallet was gone.
formula.nota: interrupción en past simple: el giro

filas.texto: The rain was tapping on the windows.
Was about to / was going to + interrupción
I was about to pay when…

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I was about to paying when I realised my wallet was gone.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I was about to pay when I realised my wallet was gone.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Was about to va seguido del verbo en forma base (pay), no de -ing.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Little I knew that she would become my partner.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Little did I know that she would become my partner.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Little al inicio pide inversión con did, y el verbo vuelve a forma base: little did I know.

situacion.contexto: Tom le cuenta a Sara cómo conoció a su socia.

dialogo.texto: It was raining, and the café was nearly empty. I was about to pay when I realised my wallet was gone.
dialogo.traduccion: Llovía y el café estaba casi vacío. Iba a pagar cuando me di cuenta de que mi cartera había desaparecido.

dialogo.texto: Oh no! What did you do?
dialogo.traduccion: ¡Ay, no! ¿Qué hiciste?

dialogo.texto: I was going to call the police, but then a woman handed me my wallet.
dialogo.traduccion: Iba a llamar a la policía, pero entonces una mujer me entregó la cartera.

dialogo.texto: Really? Who was she?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿En serio? ¿Quién era?

dialogo.texto: Little did I know, she would become my business partner.
dialogo.traduccion: Yo no tenía ni idea de que se convertiría en mi socia.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué pensaba hacer Tom al ver que no estaba su cartera?
item.feedback: Tom dice «I was going to call the police, but then a woman handed me my wallet»: la mujer interrumpió su intención.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase presenta bien una escena de fondo y el hecho que la rompe?
guiada.texto: Sara is drafting the opening of her anecdote. She wants a background scene in the past continuous, followed by a sudden event in the past simple, without mixing the tenses.
opciones: The café was nearly empty when a woman sat down at my table.
The café had been nearly empty when a woman was sitting down at my table.
The café was nearly empty when a woman sits down at my table.
The café nearly emptied when a woman was sat down at my table.
guiada.feedback: La escena de fondo va en past continuous (was nearly empty, aquí como estado) y el hecho que la rompe en past simple (sat down). Las demás mezclan tiempos sin motivo.
guiada.pista: Fondo en pasado; hecho que interrumpe en past simple.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Iba a llamar a la policía al llegar a casa, pero ella me devolvió la cartera.»
guiada.texto: I was ___ to call the police as soon as I got home, but then the woman smiled and handed back my wallet, still warm from her pocket.
guiada.feedback: Was going to + verbo base expresa una intención del pasado que no se cumple; as soon as I got home descarta was about to, que exige un momento inmediato.
guiada.pista: Intención pasada: was ___ to + verbo base.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Yo no tenía ni idea de que se convertiría en mi socia.»
guiada.respuesta: Little did I know that she would become my partner
guiada.feedback: Little al inicio exige inversión (did I know) y would anticipa el desenlace desde el pasado.
guiada.pista: Little va primero, seguido del auxiliar did y el sujeto.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la parte de la anécdota que construye.
pares: The rain was tapping on the windows.
Escena de fondo en past continuous
Suddenly, a woman sat down at my table.
Hecho que rompe la escena
I was about to pay when it dawned on me.
Intención interrumpida por un giro
Little did I know that she would help me.
Desenlace anticipado con would
practica.feedback: Cada frase ocupa un lugar distinto de la anécdota: fondo, hecho, giro y desenlace.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige cuál es el giro de esta anécdota.
practica.audio: I was standing in the queue at the station café, tapping my foot, when I realised that my train was about to leave. I was going to run for it, but the man in front of me turned to face me and handed me his ticket. “I'm not going anywhere,” he said. Little did I know that he worked at the company where I had an interview the next day and, as luck would have it, he would be one of the people asking the questions.
opciones: The kind stranger turns out to be linked to the narrator's interview.
The stranger turns out to be an old friend of the narrator.
The narrator misses the train after all and cancels the interview.
The ticket turns out to be for a train going the wrong way.
practica.feedback: El giro llega con «Little did I know»: el desconocido trabaja en la empresa de la entrevista y estará en el tribunal. Nada indica que fuera amigo ni que perdiera el tren.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Yo no tenía ni idea de que el hombre del banco me cambiaría la vida.»
practica.texto: It was a perfectly ordinary Tuesday. ___ did I know that the quiet man on the bench would change my life.
practica.feedback: Little did I know es la fórmula fija que anuncia un giro; al inicio exige inversión con did.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe una anécdota de unas 150 palabras con escena, giro y desenlace.
evaluacion.texto: Situación: una tarde de lluvia en la biblioteca de tu barrio. Ibas a devolver un libro cuando viste una nota con un número de teléfono entre las páginas. Ibas a tirarla, pero llamaste. Giro: la persona que contestó resultó ser tu futura socia. Escribe la anécdota en primera persona, de unas 150 palabras, con: escena de fondo, hecho que la rompe, was about to, was going to y un desenlace con Little did I know y would.
evaluacion.respuesta: It was a grey afternoon, and the rain was tapping on the windows of the library. I was about to return a book when I noticed a small note between the pages. Suddenly, my curiosity woke up. It was a phone number, and below it someone had written: “Call me if you find this.” I was going to throw the note away, but then I remembered how quiet the library could feel on a wet day, so I phoned. A woman answered at once. “Finally,” she said, laughing. “I left it there three years ago, as a joke.” We talked for an hour. Little did I know that she would become my business partner, and that we would open a small shop together. To my relief, the shop was an immediate success, and the note is still on the wall.
aceptadas: It was a rainy evening, and the wind was blowing hard outside the station. A few people were waiting quietly in the dark. I was about to get on the last bus when it dawned on me that my wallet was not in my bag. My heart was beating very fast. I was going to ask the driver for help, but a young woman handed me a ticket. “Don't worry,” she said. “Buy me a coffee one day.” I thanked her and sat by the window. Little did I know that I would meet her again. Two weeks later, she came into my new office, and she would become my best friend for the rest of my life, and my business partner too.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena anécdota abre con una escena en pasado continuo, la rompe con un hecho, usa was about to / was going to y anticipa el final con would (Little did I know…).

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el narrador sobre el resultado de la entrevista.
evaluacion.audio: It was a wet Sunday, and the train to Bristol was packed. I was sitting by the window, tapping my foot on the floor, when a man across from me dropped his wallet. I was about to call out when I noticed a card sticking out of it: “If lost, please return to Mr Hall.” I handed it back and thought nothing more of it. Little did I know that Mr Hall owned the company where I had applied for a job. As luck would have it, he remembered my face on the day of the interview, and within a month I had signed my contract.
opciones: That a small act of kindness helped the narrator get the job.
That Mr Hall gave the narrator the job only as a favour, despite a weak interview.
That the interview had been arranged in advance by Mr Hall.
That the narrator had known who Mr Hall was all along.
evaluacion.feedback: El narrador no lo dice, pero «he remembered my face» y el contrato un mes después sugieren que el gesto amable ayudó; el texto no habla de un favor ni de una entrevista amañada.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Iba a salir cuando caí en la cuenta de que no había enviado el contrato.»
evaluacion.texto: I was about to leave the office when it ___ on me that I had never sent the contract, and the client was waiting for it.
evaluacion.feedback: It dawned on me es la expresión fija para darse cuenta de algo de golpe; no admite otro verbo en esta construcción.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué efecto busca el narrador con el arranque de este texto?
evaluacion.texto: It was an ordinary Tuesday. The rain was tapping on the windows, and I was halfway through my second coffee, thinking about nothing more serious than dinner. Nothing, absolutely nothing, suggested that by six o'clock I would be standing on a ferry with a stranger's suitcase in my hands.
opciones: To build tension by contrasting a calm scene with what follows.
To prepare the reader for a funny, light-hearted anecdote.
To show that the narrator is bored by an ordinary life.
To explain how the narrator came to be on a ferry.
evaluacion.feedback: La escena tranquila (martes, lluvia, café) contrasta con el desenlace anunciado con would: así se crea expectación sin revelar el giro. No es una anécdota cómica ni explica el viaje.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Caí en la cuenta de que mi paraguas seguía en el tren.»
repaso.respuesta: It dawned on me that my umbrella was still on the train
repaso.feedback: It dawned on me introduce el descubrimiento; después, that + la cláusula con el hecho en pasado (was still on the train).

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender la frase final de la narradora?
repaso.texto: We had booked the house months in advance, and we were looking forward to a quiet week. As luck would have it, the only other guests were two people from our own street, and, to my relief, nobody mentioned my brother's wedding speech. Little did I know that they had been told to keep quiet about it.
opciones: That the others knew about the speech and avoided the subject.
That the two guests had not heard anything about the wedding.
That the narrator wanted the guests to mention the speech.
That her brother had asked her to keep the secret.
repaso.feedback: Que les hubieran pedido callar implica que conocían el asunto: su silencio no era ignorancia, sino discreción. El alivio de la narradora era prematuro.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Para mi alivio, el autobús también iba tarde, así que no había perdido nada.»
repaso.texto: I ran all the way to the stop, sure that I had missed the last bus. To my ___, the bus was late too, so I had not missed anything after all.
repaso.feedback: To my relief es la expresión fija para indicar que algo salió mejor de lo temido; no admite otra palabra.

classes.objetivo: Contar una anécdota familiar completa (hábito, escena, hecho, giro y desenlace) con secuencia de tiempos precisa y responder con naturalidad a las preguntas del público.

vocabulario.es: salir el tiro por la culata

ensenanza.en: At every family reunion, my uncle would hold his audience with the same story, while the distant relatives pretended never to have heard it.
ensenanza.es: En cada reunión familiar, mi tío tenía cautivo a su público con la misma historia, mientras los parientes lejanos fingían no haberla oído nunca.
ensenanza.nota: Would + verbo base abre la anécdota con un hábito del pasado; aquí una acción que se repetía.

ensenanza.en: My grandmother had been planning for weeks to play a prank on the whole family, and nobody suspected a thing.
ensenanza.es: Mi abuela llevaba semanas planeando gastarle una broma a toda la familia, y nadie sospechaba nada.
ensenanza.nota: Had been planning: una actividad en curso antes del momento que se cuenta; da el giro.

ensenanza.en: Just as I was about to blow out the candles, the punchline of her joke arrived: the cake was made of bread.
ensenanza.es: Justo cuando iba a soplar las velas, llegó el remate de su broma: el pastel estaba hecho de pan.
ensenanza.nota: Was about to + verbo se interrumpe con un hecho; el hecho que rompe la escena llega en past simple.

ensenanza.en: Good storytellers tend to embellish, and it is easy to get carried away, so keep only the details that serve the story.
ensenanza.es: Los buenos narradores tienden a adornar, y es fácil dejarse llevar, así que conserva solo los detalles que sirven a la historia.
ensenanza.nota: Embellish es adornar un relato; get carried away, pasarse de la raya por entusiasmo.

ensenanza.en: If the prank were to backfire, the whole family would be ready to see the funny side, as they always were.
ensenanza.es: Si la broma saliera mal, toda la familia estaría dispuesta a verle el lado gracioso, como siempre.
ensenanza.nota: If + were to + verbo base plantea una hipótesis poco probable; la familia reaccionaría con humor.

ensenanza.en: When the story ended, the whole audience would burst out laughing, and someone always asked, “Did you really eat it all?”
ensenanza.es: Cuando la historia terminaba, todo el público se echaba a reír, y alguien siempre preguntaba: «¿De verdad te lo comiste todo?»
ensenanza.nota: Las preguntas del público usan did + verbo base: Did you really eat…? Responde con una frase corta.

explicacion.titulo: Contar la anécdota en la reunión
explicacion.texto: Contar una anécdota en una reunión junta todo lo aprendido. Abre con un hábito o una escena mostrada (At every reunion, my uncle would…; The kitchen smelled of coffee…). Rompe la escena con un hecho en past simple o con was about to; da el giro mirando hacia atrás (had been planning) y anticipa el final con Little did I know… + would. Cierra con una frase corta o un fragmento (Silence. Then laughter.). Después, responde al público con naturalidad: un eco, un marcador (Anyway, To be honest) y respuestas cortas.

formula.texto: At every reunion, my uncle would tell…
formula.nota: escena o hábito: would / used to

formula.texto: I was about to cut the cake when…
formula.nota: hecho que la rompe, en past simple

formula.texto: Little did we know that… had been planning…
formula.nota: giro mirando atrás y desenlace anticipado

filas.texto: Used to / would, past continuous, sentidos
I was about to cut the cake when…
Had been + -ing, Little did I know
…had been planning the prank for weeks.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I opened the door and I see my grandmother with the cake.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I opened the door and saw my grandmother with the cake.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En una anécdota en pasado no se mezcla el presente: todos los verbos de la línea principal van en past simple.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Did you really ate the whole cake?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Did you really eat the whole cake?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Tras did el verbo vuelve a la forma base: did you eat, no did you ate.

situacion.contexto: En la reunión familiar, Ana cuenta una anécdota de su abuela y Leo le hace preguntas.

dialogo.texto: The kitchen smelled of coffee, and I was about to cut the cake when I noticed the candles had gone out.
dialogo.traduccion: La cocina olía a café y yo iba a cortar el pastel cuando vi que las velas se habían apagado.

dialogo.texto: Had they? Why?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Sí? ¿Por qué?

dialogo.texto: Little did I know, my grandmother had been planning a prank for weeks. The cake was made of bread!
dialogo.traduccion: No tenía ni idea de que mi abuela llevaba semanas planeando una broma. ¡El pastel era de pan!

dialogo.texto: No way! Did you eat it?
dialogo.traduccion: ¡No puede ser! ¿Te lo comiste?

dialogo.texto: I did. Silence. Then everyone started laughing.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Silencio. Luego todos empezaron a reír.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué había preparado la abuela de Ana?

opciones.es: Una broma: el pastel estaba hecho de pan.

item.feedback: Ana dice que su abuela llevaba semanas planeando una broma y que el pastel era de pan.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase muestra que la broma se preparó mucho antes de la escena?
guiada.texto: Ana is telling the story of her grandmother's prank. She wants the audience to understand that the preparations began long before the cake reached the table, and she must choose the right tense for that earlier background.
opciones: Little did we know that my grandmother had been planning the prank for weeks.
Little did we know that my grandmother was planning the prank for weeks.
Little did we know that my grandmother planned the prank for weeks.
Little did we know that my grandmother has been planning the prank for weeks.
guiada.feedback: Had been planning sitúa una actividad en curso antes del momento que se cuenta; was planning, planned y has been planning no marcan esa anterioridad.
guiada.pista: Busca el past perfect continuous: lo que duraba antes del giro.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Iba a soplar las velas cuando se apagaron las luces.»
guiada.texto: Everybody was singing, and I was about to ___ out the candles when the lights went off and somebody laughed in the dark.
guiada.feedback: Blow out the candles es la colocación para soplar las velas; was about to va seguido del verbo en forma base.
guiada.pista: Verbo base que se usa con las velas de un pastel.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Cuando terminó la historia, todos se echaron a reír.»
guiada.respuesta: When the story ended, everyone burst out laughing
guiada.feedback: El hecho principal va en past simple (ended, burst); burst out laughing se mantiene junto como expresión fija.
guiada.pista: La cláusula temporal va primero; burst out laughing al final.
aceptadas: Everyone burst out laughing when the story ended

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué revela la reacción del público.
practica.audio: My uncle cleared his throat, and the whole table fell silent. “At every reunion,” he began, “I promise myself not to tell this story. And every year, I get carried away.” The audience sighed, because they had heard it many times, and yet nobody left the table. By the punchline, even the distant relatives were crying with laughter.
opciones: They know the story well but still enjoy hearing it.
They are bored and hope that he will finish soon.
They are hearing the story for the very first time.
They dislike the way he embellishes the story.
practica.feedback: Suspiran porque ya la conocen, pero nadie se marcha y hasta los parientes lejanos terminan llorando de risa: disfrutan de la costumbre.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Pasamos semanas planeando la broma y nadie sospechaba nada.»
practica.texto: It was my cousin's idea, and we spent weeks ___ the prank in secret, although nobody in the house suspected a thing.
practica.feedback: Spend weeks + -ing es la estructura natural; planning es la colocación más habitual con prank, y preparing también es posible.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con el paso de la anécdota al que pertenece.
pares: At every reunion, my uncle would tell the story.
Hábito del pasado que abre la escena
The kitchen smelled of coffee.
Escena mostrada con un detalle del olfato
I was about to cut the cake when the lights went out.
Hecho que rompe la escena
Did you really eat it all?
Pregunta del público
practica.feedback: Cada frase cumple un paso distinto: hábito, escena mostrada, hecho que interrumpe y pregunta del público.

evaluacion.consigna: Cuenta la anécdota (unas 170 palabras) y responde a las dos preguntas del público.
evaluacion.texto: Situación: reunión familiar en casa de tu abuela. Cada verano tu tía Mia contaba la historia del día que perdió su paraguas en la estación. Un año, iba a empezar cuando un desconocido entró en el jardín con un paraguas viejo: era el hombre que lo había encontrado hacía treinta años y llevaba todo ese tiempo buscándola. Cuenta la anécdota (unas 170 palabras) con: un hábito o escena del pasado (used to / would), un hecho con was about to, un giro con had been o Little did we know y un final corto. Después responde a dos preguntas del público: «Did you recognise him?» y «What did your aunt say?».
evaluacion.respuesta:
Every summer, the whole family used to meet at my grandmother's house. The kitchen smelled of coffee, and the relatives were all talking at once. My aunt Mia would always tell the same story about the day she lost her umbrella at the station. That year, she was about to start it again when a stranger walked into the garden, holding an old umbrella. Nobody recognised him. Silence. Then my aunt stood up and put her hand to her face. “It's mine,” she whispered. He had been looking for her for thirty years, and he had kept the umbrella in his house all that time. Little did we know that he would stay for dinner, and that he would become part of the family.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a neighbour.
What did your aunt say? Fair enough, she said. Tonight, for once, we will hear a new story.
aceptadas:
When I was a child, we would all meet at my grandmother's house on Sundays. The kitchen smelled of bread, and the relatives were laughing in the garden. My aunt Mia used to tell the same story about the day she lost her umbrella at the station. One Sunday, she was about to begin when a tall man walked into the garden with an umbrella in his hand. Nobody knew him. Silence. Then my aunt smiled and opened her arms. “That's my umbrella,” she said. He had been searching for her for thirty years, and he had never given up. Little did I know that he would become my uncle's best friend.
Did you recognise him? No, I didn't. I thought he was a friend of my uncle.
What did your aunt say? Honestly, she said nothing. She just hugged him.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena versión abre con hábito o escena, rompe con un hecho o was about to, da el giro con had been o Little did we know y responde a las dos preguntas del público (reconocerlo y qué dijo tu tía) con respuestas cortas.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el final sobre la actitud de la familia.
evaluacion.audio: Every year, at the family reunion, my uncle Carlos would tell the same story about the night he met my aunt. He would embellish it a little more each time, until the rain became a storm and the walk became a mountain climb. The distant relatives would smile politely, and my cousins would count the new details. Yet nobody ever stopped him. When he reached the punchline, the whole table burst out laughing, even those who could have told it word for word. Last year he forgot the ending. Nobody helped him. For once, we all just wanted to hear him find it.
opciones: That the family cares more about the tradition than about the story itself.
That the family had finally grown tired of the story.
That the uncle was losing his memory and they were worried.
That the cousins secretly preferred a different story.
evaluacion.feedback: Nadie lo ayudó porque querían oírlo encontrar el final: lo que valoran es la costumbre de escucharlo, no los detalles de la historia.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Adorna sus historias: cada vez que las cuenta, el pez crece.»
evaluacion.texto: Every time he tells it, the fish gets bigger. He likes to ___ his stories a little, and nobody minds.
evaluacion.feedback: Embellish es la palabra precisa para adornar un relato; exaggerate y embroider también son posibles, pero embellish subraya el adorno más que la exageración.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender la pausa de Ana en esta conversación?
evaluacion.texto: “Did you really eat it?” asked Leo. “Every bit,” said Ana. “Even the candles?” “Well...” She looked at the ceiling. “Let's say I got carried away.” For a second nobody laughed. Then the whole table burst out laughing, and Leo laughed too.
opciones: That she is exaggerating to keep the audience laughing.
That she has forgotten what happened that night.
That she is embarrassed about what she ate.
That she does not want to answer his question.
evaluacion.feedback: La pausa y «Let's say I got carried away» revelan que adorna la respuesta para divertir; la risa posterior confirma que el público entiende el juego.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Toda la mesa se echó a reír al oír el remate.»
repaso.respuesta: The whole table burst out laughing at the punchline
repaso.feedback: Burst out laughing se mantiene junto; at the punchline indica el momento exacto de la reacción.

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor sobre las historias familiares?
repaso.texto: Family stories are rarely accurate. Every retelling embellishes them, drops the awkward details and improves the punchline, until the tale says more about the family than about the event. Yet that, surely, is the point: nobody at a reunion wants a report; they want to hear themselves described, a little taller and a little funnier than they were.
opciones: That they need not be strictly accurate to be worth telling.
That they should be checked against the real facts.
That they reveal more about the family than the event, which is a problem.
That a good punchline matters more than any other detail.
repaso.feedback: «Yet that, surely, is the point» defiende que la inexactitud es lo que da sentido a estas historias: no buscan informar, sino reflejar a la familia, y el autor no lo lamenta.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «La broma podría haber salido mal, pero mi tía supo verle el lado gracioso.»
repaso.texto: The prank could easily have ___, but luckily my aunt was able to see the funny side and laughed with everybody else.
repaso.feedback: Backfire describe algo que sale al revés de lo previsto; failed no expresa ese efecto contrario y suena menos natural.

notes: Revisión independiente C1 (30-09-2026): ajustadas las claves ambiguas (n10-c5 guiada: eco Did she?/Does she? desambiguado; n10-c9 guiada: was going to frente a was about to/planning) y los distractores de contradicción directa reescritos como near-misses (c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7, c8, c9, c10).

Corregido: c7 e3 decía 'tres palabras' (She did not go = 4); c8 e0 audio con cronología incoherente (Years earlier vs the night I left); c8 e1 convertido a escuchar (el mapa pide audio); c9 r0 copiaba literal la enseñanza; c10 e0 sin evidencia para la segunda pregunta del público y con pronombre-concordancia permisivo.
Español neutro: cotilleo→chisme, tarta→pastel; consignas de completar con traducción más completa.

Rúbricas c6 e0, c7 e0 (una sola anteposición basta, como pide la consigna), c8 e3, c9 e0 y c10 e0 ampliadas con variantes naturales (blushed/bit her lip, 'had already been waiting', 'little did I realise', respuestas 'nobody did'); probadas con textos naturales y arbitrarios.
